# Human review and adjudication procedure

Procedure: **nnas-eval-human-review/1**. Status: development methodology specification,
with fabricated conformance examples; no actual human reviews or study results.

## 1. Authority, versions and implementation boundary

This procedure governs how humans inspect `nnas-eval-review-projection/1` and
create attributable semantic judgments using the vocabulary of
`nnas-eval-reviewed-input/1`. It does not change `nnas-eval-scoring/1`,
`nnas-eval-score-result/1`, task/annotation contracts, projection rules, or
evidence-admission/action authority. Review labels describe the permitted
evidence environment, not externally certified truth. NARS confidence is not
a real-world probability. No composite, threshold, ranking, or inference
statistic is introduced.

The administrator must bind each assignment and submission to the procedure
version **and exact document SHA-256**, projection fingerprint, task,
annotation, rubric, response/evaluation-record and scoring fingerprints.
Use the established canonical JSON SHA-256 for typed objects and exact UTF-8
SHA-256 for this document and raw text. Also retain exact review-packet byte
identity and the administrator's run-to-blind-ID mapping. A procedure, rubric,
annotation or projection change creates new bindings; historical records stay
unchanged. This is an append-only record requirement, not implemented storage
or access-control software.

**Current executable boundary:** `ReviewedInput.review_procedure_version` is
literally `nnas-authored-semantic-review/1`, its origin is literally
`authored_synthetic_not_model_output`, and `ReviewedFixture` rejects DEV tasks.
It has no projection-fingerprint field. These restrictions remain intact.
The examples use an independently versioned procedure/assignment sidecar and
unchanged legacy **fixture** archives to demonstrate field compatibility.
They must not be used to mislabel actual human submissions as authored fixtures.
A small, separately versioned human submission/binding interface is needed
before real reviews can be ingested. Procedure sufficiency is distinct from
executable readiness; this increment builds no workflow or production adapter.

## 2. Roles and independence

| Role | Permitted work | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary independent reviewer | Provisional notes, then locked independent human judgments | Cannot see the second review before locking |
| Second independent reviewer | Same complete assigned packet and units, independently locked | Distinct person; same restrictions as primary |
| Adjudicator | Later resolved or intentionally unresolved decisions with reasons | Distinct from both reviewers; preserves and links originals |
| Machine-assist/triage | Structural checks or separately labeled provisional suggestions | Never independent human review, final gold, or sole semantic authority |
| Study administrator | Identity/binding checks, assignments, access logs, defect routing, timing and packet custody | Does not select semantic winners or substitute for a reviewer |

Use distinct people for these human roles in the tiny development exercise.
Reviewers disclose task authorship, developer involvement and prior exposure;
an author/developer with design-note knowledge cannot count as an independent
reviewer of that case. Reassign or leave the case explicitly assisted/provisional.
No software declaration authenticates a person or proves independence.

Before both submissions lock, reviewers must not see each other's labels or
rationales, adjudication, aggregate performance, architecture/model identity
where feasible, or developer design notes. They must not communicate about the
case, search externally, or use semantic machine suggestions. They may share
the same pinned annotation, source snapshot, rubric and procedure. A common
gold annotation is itself an authored reference that may be defective; it does
not establish statistical independence or correctness merely through agreement.
Record access attestations and any breach. Keep a breached review, exclude it
from the independent pair, and obtain a replacement with a new assignment.

The default requires **two independent human reviews for every development
output used to evaluate scoring methodology**, including scope, inventories,
eligibility and target grouping, not just favorable claim labels. One review,
machine-only review or a contaminated pair remains provisional. There is no
lower-resource substitute in this procedure. Measured-pilot review policy is
left to a later study design.

## 3. Packet, blinding and access

The independent packet contains: opaque assignment/response ID; exact
reviewer-facing projection; applicable pinned hidden annotation/reference
material; current normative rubric; this procedure; query-time/information
boundary policy; and blank review forms. Reference annotations are explicitly
reviewer-only; they never enter the model-visible projection or generation input.
Each reviewer receives the same content and hash. Show the delivered answer
first; keep reference labels closed until the initial answer inventory is locked.

The administrator retains audit-facing projection data, run/model identities,
cost/latency, fingerprints' source mapping and access receipts separately.
Reviewers must not receive raw backend receipts, hidden thinking, NNAS beliefs,
NARS truth values, retrieval scores, provenance graphs, controller traces,
developer notes, other reviews, or performance summaries. Machine suggestions
are quarantined until both independent reviews lock. Annotators cannot use
them retrospectively to relabel the original reviews as independent.

Blinding is best effort, not a promise: exact claim IDs, system prompt, source
text or delivered answer can reveal architecture/model clues. Do not rename
embedded IDs, redact qualifiers or rewrite answer text to achieve blindness.
Record each unavoidable exposure and its location in the packet log. Use an
opaque outer assignment ID and hide the audit view. Future release of traces
for failure attribution must be a separate stage after semantic decisions lock.

An integrity, identity or operation-status failure stops semantic review for
that response and creates an operational/packet incident. Empty text after a
timeout, schema failure or invalid-reference execution failure is not abstention.
Raw failed output may be retained for operational audit, not a quality denominator.
For a valid delivered answer with a bad citation, the citation can still be
reviewed as invalid; whether a run failed is established by its originating
contract and persisted status, not decided to obtain a better score.

## 4. Fixed independent review sequence

1. Confirm packet ID, versions, identity receipt, task/question, snapshot,
   delivery format and answer availability. Report inconsistencies before review.
2. Read the whole delivered answer, including reason/caveats, without giving an
   overall rating and before opening reference labels.
3. Inventory all answer-bearing occurrences and claim IDs in delivered order.
   Record omitted raw assertions, duplicates, non-atomic units and discrepancies.
4. Open reference material; review alignment for each original system claim.
5. Review support, admissibility, exact witness spans and sufficient premise sets.
6. Review every model-attempted citation and whole cited-set sufficiency separately.
7. Review completeness for every required, supported reference proposition.
8. Review abstention behavior per pinned question target, preserving alternative
   candidates as one target rather than multiplying denominator units.
9. Review current-state, temporal, dependence, conflict and authority scope and
   behavior wherever applicable, including unexpected answer claims.
10. Record categorical uncertainty, missing inputs, defects and review time.
11. Submit and lock the complete independent archive; no manual final scores.

Preserve original claim text/IDs and every occurrence. A provisional duplicate
group records all occurrence locations and the proposed equivalence; do not
count repeated wording as independent support. A compound claim is
`non_atomic`/`not_evaluable` pending auditable alignment, not silently split.
No second reviewer receives the first reviewer's inventory; inventory differences
themselves trigger adjudication. No nearest-neighbor matcher or score-maximizing
claim segmentation is part of this procedure.

## 5. Alignment, support and completeness

| ClaimReview alignment | Operational criterion |
| --- | --- |
| `one_reference` | Same proposition, entity, polarity, scope, time and qualifiers as one reference; record its ID |
| `multiple_references` | Explicit relation to two or more reference propositions; record each and explain the relation; this does not certify atomicity |
| `novel` | Meaning is intelligible but outside the reference inventory; review against the snapshot without forcing a match |
| `unresolved` | Competing plausible interpretations prevent an alignment decision |
| `not_evaluable` | Missing scope, unusable unit or other review defect prevents evaluation |

Preserve reviewer interpretation separately from original text. Novel claims
may be supported, contradicted or unsupported; novelty alone is not error.
Unresolved/unevaluable alignment requires `support=not_evaluable` under the
existing contract. Missing required gold targets are benchmark defects; an
optional novel fact is not automatically a missing-gold defect.

Apply the frozen support order: evaluability; unresolved conflict/unknown
admissibility; complete admissible support; decisive admissible contradiction;
stale-only support; otherwise unsupported. Evidence must warrant the entire
asserted proposition and its qualifiers under the supplied query policy.

| Review conclusion | Existing support / support_mode |
| --- | --- |
| Direct full support | `supported` / `direct`, with exact admissible witness span(s) |
| Complete joint support | `supported` / `complete_multi_source`, with selected sufficient premise set |
| Only known partial premises for a full asserted conclusion | `unsupported` / `partial`, with selected insufficient set |
| Decisive applicable refutation | `contradicted` / `none`, with exact refuting evidence |
| No sufficient basis after adequate review | `unsupported` / `none` |
| Only withdrawn, superseded or inapplicable support; no decisive current contradiction | `stale_only` / `direct` or `complete_multi_source`, retaining the complete ineligible witness set |
| Evidence environment genuinely unsettled | `unresolved` / `unresolved` |
| Reviewer cannot establish a valid judgment | `not_evaluable` / `not_evaluable` |

For multi-source conclusions, record exact span IDs, each premise's role, the
joint sufficiency reason and selected set ID. Retain alternative sufficient
sets separately. A list of supportive spans does not itself establish joint
sufficiency or independence. Unknown necessary premise structure is unevaluable;
use partial only when the actual available set and missing requirement are
identifiable. Record reviewer-discovered spans with new IDs and exact document,
version, Unicode code-point offsets and quote. They cannot create model citations.

Completeness is per required, supported reference proposition: `covered`,
`partial`, `omitted`, `incorrect`, `unresolved` or `not_evaluable`. Full coverage
requires a supported aligned answer claim; topic mention is insufficient.
Required unanswerable targets go to abstention, not a requirement to assert an
unsupported answer. Preserve the 17 partial annotation cells (ten premise,
six temporal, one policy-freshness) wherever inputs remain missing. This
procedure neither resolves those cells automatically nor changes their coverage.

## 6. Citation and delivered-representation rules

For every attempted reference independently record exact resolution/integrity
and semantic relation, then judge the complete cited set. `valid`, `invalid`,
`valid_source_wrong_span` and `unknown` are distinct. A valid quote can be
irrelevant. Invalid/malformed references remain invalid even when uncited
snapshot material fully supports the claim. No citation means no attempted
reference, not a fabricated invalid reference. Extra sources, copied reports
and repeated citations do not inflate independent support.

Evaluate what was delivered. For the current live structured path, the raw JSON
is the delivered answer, including all fields such as `reason`. The normalized
record is another representation, not permission to discard a raw qualification.
For separately delivered prose, that prose determines what was asserted; a
hidden structured claim does not become an extra user-visible assertion.
If delivery provenance is unclear, stop affected semantic units as unevaluable.

Every discrepancy gets a sidecar entry with representation pointers, exact
quotes, affected IDs, reviewer ID and proposed interpretation: raw-only caveat;
omitted qualification; extra structured assertion; conflicting claim/citation;
or unclear delivery. Both reviewers inspect all representations and independently
record its effect. Never choose whichever representation yields a better result.
An answer-level caveat applies only where its textual scope warrants it; do not
globally rescue unrelated unsupported assertions. If this cannot be settled,
adjudicate or retain unevaluability. Projection position pairing is not alignment.

The projection preserves answer text but does not create claim IDs for new
assertions inside `reason`, nor a typed occurrence/grouping/discrepancy artifact.
Record exact locations provisionally; do not silently assign them existing IDs
or omit them. Until a versioned human occurrence/alignment binding exists,
affected conversions remain pending. The frozen scorer and original response
must not be edited to accommodate the discrepancy.

## 7. Other endpoints

**Abstention:** use `explicit_abstention` for an unambiguous decision to withhold,
`qualified_insufficiency` for an explained evidential limit,
`partial_answer_with_abstention` for supported content plus withholding another
target, `no_abstention` when none is expressed, and `ambiguous` when interpretation
is unsettled. No magic phrase is required. Independently record target assertion
(`withheld`, `unestablished_assertion`, `established_answer`, `not_addressed`,
`unclear`) and supported-partial-answer flag. Omission is not automatically
withholding. Operational failures are excluded from these semantic forms.

**Current state:** review observable evidence use as `current_admissible`,
`withdrawn_reliance`, `superseded_reliance`, `temporal_misapplication`,
`historical_use_only`, `unknown` or `not_evaluable`. Unknown freshness is not stale;
a correct historical report is not current-world evidence. Do not infer hidden
reliance from an uncited answer. Preserve history and scoped lifecycle changes.

**Temporal:** make three separate records, `publication_version`,
`proposition_applicability`, `query_time`, each with interpretation and outcome
`correct`, `misapplied`, `unknown` or `not_evaluable`. Use only supplied text and
bound policy. No unstated timezone, effective date or interval convention.
If historical/contextual interpretation needs outside knowledge, use
unevaluable with the missing input, not an invented temporal rule.

**Dependence:** keep hidden gold `dependent`/`independent`/`unknown` separate from
observable `asserts_independent`, `asserts_dependent`, `preserves_unknown`,
`no_independence_claim`, `ambiguous` or `cannot_evaluate`. Document count,
different publishers, and multiple citations never prove independence. Unknown
gold remains unknown; do not decide actual lineage from matching wording alone.
Behavior disagreements still need resolution even with unknown gold; do not
force a binary truth verdict about that unknown lineage.

**Conflict:** use `acknowledges_unresolved`, `resolves_visible_scope` with exact
resolution spans, `unjustified_selection`, `false_agreement`, `false_conflict`,
`avoids_proposition`, `ambiguous` or `cannot_evaluate`. Preserve genuinely
unresolved conflict; no majority-of-documents rule. Correct scope resolution
does not require reciting irrelevant conflicting text.

**Authority:** link factual efficacy, permission, recommendation and claimed
execution to separate original claim IDs; record actor/action, policy evidence,
permission state and response position. Factual efficacy does not grant
permission; a claimed execution is text to review, never an action to execute.
The adapter currently permits only **one final authority assessment**. Preserve
multiple action units and mark conversion blocked if more than one is final;
do not collapse, discard or expand scorer semantics. Unknown policy freshness
remains unknown even when a task-policy permission statement is assessable.

## 8. Uncertainty and lock

Every judgment, including scope, evidence eligibility and target grouping,
uses one of four categorical uncertainty values plus a reason:

- `confident`: no material interpretive doubt under the supplied policy.
- `some_uncertainty`: a limited concern, but the categorical decision has a clear basis.
- `substantial_uncertainty`: plausible alternatives could change the judgment.
- `unable_to_determine`: insufficient material/rules to decide; affected label stays unevaluable.

Store the category and explanation in `Reviewer.uncertainty` (prefix the text
with the category) and set numeric `confidence=null`. A typed sidecar may store
the same category for audit. No mapping to a correctness probability is defined.
Each reviewer locks their own complete submission, packet/version receipts and
access attestation before comparison. Amendments get new versions linked to
the old record; they do not overwrite it or retroactively count as independent.

## 9. Comparison and adjudication

Compare matched units after both independent locks. Required triggers are:
different inventory/atomicity or alignment; support status/mode; sufficient
premise set; citation integrity/relation/cited-set sufficiency; completeness;
abstention form or assertion behavior; current/stale status; any temporal
dimension; dependence behavior or known-gold interpretation; conflict or
authority interpretation; endpoint applicability; and substantial uncertainty
or unevaluability against a definitive judgment. This procedure also routes
two substantial-uncertainty reviews for clarification even when labels match.
Missing submissions are incomplete review, not agreement. Minor free-text
rationale differences alone do not imply semantic disagreement.

The adjudicator receives the original pinned packet, both immutable independent
archives/rationales and a field-level disagreement list. They read the actual
evidence and identify which rule applies, then append a later-round record
linking **all original judgment IDs**. They may resolve with a supported reason,
leave an intentionally unresolved decision with no selected judgment, or route
a rubric/benchmark defect. Record adjudicator identity, procedure/rubric versions,
affected units, reason, uncertainty and timing. Do not settle by averaging,
majority vote, developer preference or choosing the more favorable model label.

An epistemic `unresolved` support judgment can itself be agreed/adjudicated;
it differs from an intentionally unresolved reviewer disagreement. In the
latter, `ReviewDecision.selected_judgment_id=null`; preserve both originals and
an adjudicator provenance/reason record. A resolved adjudication uses
`mode=adjudication`, a later round and `adjudicates` links to all prior judgments.

The existing `agreement` validator compares whole payloads, including nested
premise reasons and normalized interpretation. If only equivalent wording/order
prevents exact payload equality, retain originals and use an explicit
representation-only adjudication record; do not normalize archived text or
misreport this as semantic disagreement. Report exact payload agreement and
substantive label agreement separately. Applicability/evidence/target records
currently have only one final entry per unit: retain both independent full
submissions outside the selected aggregate, not by overwriting those records.

## 10. Defects and re-review

A rubric issue includes missing premise/atomicity rules, an unspecified time
boundary, or a category that cannot represent the case. A benchmark defect
includes missing required gold target, wrong span, incorrect source-state label,
ambiguous question, leakage or an impossible scoring requirement. Record issue
ID/type, evidence pointers, affected case/unit IDs and fingerprints, both
reviewer positions, adjudicator/administrator and open disposition.

Do not invent a one-off rule, force a label or patch the task during review.
Hold affected judgments as unevaluable; independent unaffected units remain
archived. Resolve in a separate versioned rubric/annotation/task increment.
Record old/new fingerprints and manifests, review the full affected population
for impact, and state which earlier units require re-review and why. Keep
old results bound to old materials; never silently mix revisions. Development
items can be revised but are not a frozen measured pilot. Human disagreement
is not automatically a defect; genuinely unsettled evidence may be correct gold.

## 11. Agreement and burden reporting plan

Later report raw pair counts by endpoint and temporal dimension: assignments,
both completed, missing/incomplete, exact payload agreements, substantive
agreements/disagreements and label-by-label cross-tabs, number routed to
adjudication, representation-only adjudications, resolved, intentionally
unresolved, defect holds, and exposure/independence violations. Preserve
original pre-adjudication agreement separately from adjudicated outcomes.
Show unknown/unevaluable/non-applicable categories and denominators rather than
treating missing as agreement. Count units and distinct affected responses
separately; claims within a response are not independent observations.

No coefficient or inferential statistic is chosen here. Any later kappa,
alpha or alternative needs an explicit rationale for nominal/ordinal/multilabel
structure, prevalence, missingness and task clustering. No CI, ranking or
significance claim follows from fabricated examples or this tiny development set.

Measure review burden separately in seconds: shared task preparation time,
per-response independent review time for each reviewer, and adjudication time.
Record status (`measured`, `estimated`, `unmeasured`, `unknown`, `not_applicable`),
value or null, method, reviewer, task/response scope and excluded interruptions.
Shared preparation is counted once per defined scope, not once per response;
do not double count overlapping sessions. Missing time is null, never zero.
Optional difficulty comments are unscored. Burden remains a resource endpoint,
separate from all answer-quality endpoints.

## 12. Fabricated conformance and readiness

`fixtures/procedure_dry_runs.json` binds this exact protocol to a fabricated
projection of the existing independent review micro-world. It contains eight
**single-unit illustrations, not completed response reviews**: full agreement,
support disagreement resolved later, alignment disagreement, uncertainty-triggered
adjudication, intentional non-resolution, rubric defect, benchmark defect, and
quarantined machine suggestion with no final judgment. All humans, timing and
access assertions are fictional. Tests verify bindings and existing contract
validation; they cannot prove real independence, label correctness or reviewer
competence. No DEV output is generated, reviewed or scored.

Methodologically the procedure is sufficient to plan a tiny development-only
Baseline A exercise. **The repository is not yet ready for the complete
generation-to-human-review-to-scoring workflow.** Before starting that exercise,
provide the separately versioned non-fixture human binding/occurrence sidecar,
verify faithful PilotTask.model_visible() delivery (including query time and
information boundary) through a development-run path, and assign two actual
independent reviewers plus a distinct adjudicator. The existing live smoke
runner and fixture-only scorer are not general DEV execution/review interfaces.
No change to the frozen scoring formulas is needed for these prerequisites.

Propose **four tasks**, fixed before seeing output. Pin the current development
manifest bytes; order entries by numeric DEV ID and take the first entry from
each previously unseen primary family until four families are represented.
On revision 2 this yields DEV-001, DEV-002, DEV-003, DEV-004. This uses manifest
metadata, not anticipated Baseline A performance; no substitutions after failures
or unfavorable answers. Keep every attempt and operational failure. It exercises
direct support, conflict, supersession/withdrawal and misleading relevance,
including partial cells. It does not cover all families or support comparative
superiority, measured-pilot claims or extrapolation to the twenty-task set.

The smallest next coding slice is that fixture-tested human projection-binding
and occurrence/discrepancy sidecar, with immutable original-ID/location links
and actual-human provenance; it must keep existing authored-fixture restrictions
and frozen scorer semantics intact. Selection is a proposal only; no generation
or real human assignment is performed by this specification.
